cues.en: This is the city of Lafayette,
cues.zh: 这是拉斐特市，

cues.en: Louisiana.
cues.zh: 路易斯安那州。

cues.en: It's a pretty typical mid sized American city.
cues.zh: 这是个相当典型的中型美国城市。

cues.en: Like most American cities, it has that one nice old building that didn't get bulldozed in the sixties.
cues.zh: 和大多数美国城市一样，它有一栋漂亮的老建筑，在六十年代没被推土机铲平。

cues.en: And like most American cities, it's broke.
cues.zh: 也和大多数美国城市一样，它破产了。

cues.en: It's full of aging infrastructure in desperate need of repair and not enough money to maintain it. But unlike most American cities, Lafayette acknowledged this fact and requested the help of Strong Towns and Urban three, a consulting company that helps cities better understand the economic impact of development.
cues.zh: 到处都是老化基础设施，急需维修，却没有足够的钱来维护。但与大多数美国城市不同，拉斐特承认了这一事实，并请求 Strong Towns 和 Urban three 的帮助——这是一家帮助城市更好地理解开发经济影响的咨询公司。

cues.en: Their analysis in Lafayette uncovered a harsh reality that should be a wake up call to every municipality in North America.
cues.zh: 他们在拉斐特的分析揭示了一个严酷的现实，应该给北美每个市政当局敲响警钟。

cues.en: As well as any city emulating the American car centric style of development.
cues.zh: 以及任何效仿美国以汽车为中心开发模式的城市。

cues.en: But let's back up a bit.
cues.zh: 但我们先往回捋一捋。

cues.en: In a previous video in this series, we discussed how two identical lots in the same city have very different property tax revenue.
cues.zh: 在本系列之前的视频中，我们讨论了同一城市中两块相同地块如何产生截然不同的房产税收入。

cues.en: In this example, a 100 year old commercial block built in the traditional style of development
cues.zh: 在这个例子中，一栋按传统开发模式建造的百年商业街区

cues.en: drastically outperformed a shiny new development created in the modern car centric style.
cues.zh: 远远胜过了一个以现代汽车为中心风格建造的崭新开发区。

cues.en: But despite the differences in revenue, both blocks have the same cost to the city to maintain their infrastructure.
cues.zh: 但尽管收入有差异，两个街区维护基础设施的城市成本却是一样的。

cues.en: So by bulldozing an old block of shops to build this car centric second rate taco joint, the city was destroying its wealth.
cues.zh: 所以，推平一栋老商铺楼去建这个以汽车为中心的二流墨西哥卷饼店，城市其实是在摧毁自己的财富。

cues.en: This example alone should be enough to convince anyone that the modern car centric suburban style of development is broken, but it's worth exploring this further.
cues.zh: 仅这个例子就足以让任何人相信，以汽车为中心的现代郊区开发模式已经失灵，但值得进一步探讨。

cues.en: Does this hold up in other cities? And what happens when we bring into account the cost of servicing these properties with roads, water pipes, sewers, etcetera?
cues.zh: 这种情况在其他城市也成立吗？如果把用道路、水管、下水道等维护这些物业的成本算进去，又会怎样？

cues.en: And that brings us back to Lafayette.
cues.zh: 这就把我们带回了 Lafayette。

cues.en: This is a map of the revenue and expenses data uncovered by Urban three. So what are we looking at?
cues.zh: 这是 Urban three 揭示的收入与支出数据地图。那我们看到的是什么？

cues.en: Well, any successful business tracks its ROI, its return on investment.
cues.zh: 任何成功企业都会追踪 ROI，也就是投资回报率。

cues.en: When making a decision between two competing projects, it's critical to know which one will result in the most revenue compared to the investment put into it.
cues.zh: 在两个相互竞争的项目之间做决定时，关键是要知道哪一个带来的收入相对投入最多。

cues.en: And too many projects with a negative return on investment could bankrupt a company.
cues.zh: 投资回报为负的项目太多，可能会让一家公司破产。

cues.en: But in order to know your ROI, need to know two things. Your revenue and your expenses.
cues.zh: 但要了解 ROI，需要知道两件事：收入和支出。

cues.en: Urban three created a kind of municipal return on investment for Lafayette.
cues.zh: Urban three 为 Lafayette 创建了一种市政投资回报率。

cues.en: This map shows the municipal revenue per acre. So why per acre other than the fact that Americans can't use metric?
cues.zh: 这张图显示每英亩的市政收入。那为什么按英亩算？除了美国人不用公制之外。

cues.en: Well, every property in a city needs services and the majority of services get more expensive the more spread out they are.
cues.zh: 因为城市中每处物业都需要服务，而大多数服务越分散就越贵。

cues.en: Roads are the obvious example. The farther a parcel of land is from everything else, the more asphalt is needed to get there.
cues.zh: 道路是最明显的例子。一块土地离其他一切越远，通向那里所需的沥青就越多。

cues.en: The worst case scenario are cul de sac, which are basically just city subsidized driveways.
cues.zh: 最糟的情况是死胡同，它们基本上就是城市补贴的车道。

cues.en: This also applies to water infrastructure, sewers, and all other physical infrastructure.
cues.zh: 这也适用于供水设施、下水道以及所有其他实体基础设施。

cues.en: As well as the cost of policing, fire department coverage, and even the cost of providing education.
cues.zh: 还有治安、消防服务的成本，甚至提供教育的成本。

cues.en: But while per area revenue is quite a good approximation, Urban three wanted to fully understand these expenses,
cues.zh: 不过，虽然单位面积收入是个相当不错的近似值，Urban3 还是想彻底弄清这些开支，

cues.en: so they painstakingly
cues.zh: 于是他们不辞辛劳地

cues.en: calculated the cost of services for each parcel of land in Lafayette.
cues.zh: 逐块计算了拉法耶特每一块土地的服务成本。

cues.en: It looks something like this.
cues.zh: 结果大致是这样。

cues.en: This shows every area that's a net positive for the city in gray, and every area that's a net negative in red.
cues.zh: 图里用灰色标出对城市财政有净收益的区域，用红色标出净亏损的区域。

cues.en: And here it is in three d.
cues.zh: 下面是三维版本。

cues.en: This analysis has some fascinating
cues.zh: 这项分析得出了一些非常有趣的

cues.en: results.
cues.zh: 结论。

cues.en: The first is that downtown is wildly profitable.
cues.zh: 第一个是：市中心极其赚钱。

cues.en: This is a bit surprising because there's nothing particularly remarkable about Downtown Lafayette. It's certainly not bad,
cues.zh: 这有点出乎意料，因为拉法耶特的市中心并没有什么特别之处。它当然不差，

cues.en: but you'd never know from looking at these pictures that this is the economic engine of the city.
cues.zh: 但光看这些照片，你绝不会想到这里是整个城市的经济引擎。

cues.en: While places like this are a drain on city finances.
cues.zh: 而像这样的地方却在消耗城市财政。

cues.en: But this shouldn't be too surprising when you think about it because there's an insane amount of asphalt and infrastructure here for a very small number of shops.
cues.zh: 不过仔细想想，这并不奇怪，因为区区几家小店，就占了多得离谱的沥青路面和基础设施。

cues.en: And for some bizarre reason, the Google Street View car drove down every aisle of this parking lot.
cues.zh: 而且不知出于什么古怪的原因，Google 街景车把这片停车场的每一条通道都开了一遍。

cues.en: But since they did it over multiple years, you can move down this way
cues.zh: 正因为这是跨越多年拍摄的，你可以沿着这边往下看，

cues.en: and watch the Toys R Us go out of business.
cues.zh: 亲眼见证 Toys R Us（玩具反斗城）倒闭的过程。

cues.en: Most of these profitable gray areas are the historical neighborhoods built along the river.
cues.zh: 这些赚钱的灰色区域，大多是沿河而建的历史街区。

cues.en: But one of the biggest spikes is this place, a modern mixed use walkable neighborhood called River Ranch.
cues.zh: 但最大的峰值之一就是这里——一个名为 River Ranch 的现代混合用途步行社区。

cues.en: Places like this are a net positive for the city.
cues.zh: 像这样的地方对城市来说是净利好。

cues.en: One of the most shocking discoveries that Strong Towns discovered is that the replacement cost of all of the infrastructure in Lafayette, something that you would expect to happen over about one generation,
cues.zh: Strong Towns 最令人震惊的发现之一是，Lafayette 所有基础设施的重置成本，按理说应该在大约一代人的时间里发生，
大约是320亿美元。

cues.en: And that's just infrastructure,
cues.zh: 而这仅仅是基础设施，

cues.en: not all the other everyday costs needed to run a city.
cues.zh: 不是维持一座城市运转所需的所有其他日常成本。

cues.en: Yet the existing tax base was much smaller than that.
cues.zh: 而现有的税基比那要小得多。

cues.en: In order to bridge the difference, Strong Towns calculated that the average family in Lafayette would see their tax bill go from about $1,500
cues.zh: 为了弥合这一差距，Strong Towns 计算出拉斐特普通家庭的税单将从大约 1500 美元

cues.en: per year to $9,200
cues.zh: 每年到9,200美元

cues.en: per year. But the median household income in Lafayette was only $41,000
cues.zh: 每年。但Lafayette的家庭收入中位数只有4.1万美元

cues.en: at the time.
cues.zh: 当时。

cues.en: There's simply no way that can happen.
cues.zh: 这根本不可能发生。

cues.en: But those simple averages are hiding the bigger picture of who's subsidizing who.
cues.zh: 但这些简单的平均值掩盖了谁在补贴谁的整体图景。

cues.en: Because these gray sections are the poorer areas, while these red areas are significantly wealthier.
cues.zh: 因为灰色区域是较贫困的地区，而红色区域则富裕得多。

cues.en: So here's a fun quiz. Which of these two neighborhoods is subsidizing the other? Number one or number two?
cues.zh: 来做个有趣的小测验。这两个社区里，哪一个在补贴另一个？一号还是二号？

cues.en: Yeah. It's the first one that's subsidizing the second. The poorest people in Lafayette are consistently subsidizing wealthy suburbanites.
cues.zh: 对，就是第一类人在补贴第二类人。拉法耶特最穷的人一直在补贴富裕的郊区居民。

cues.en: But I don't wanna pick on Lafayette here. As I said at the beginning, there's nothing particularly unique about Lafayette and these results are typical for most American cities.
cues.zh: 但我不想针对拉法叶市。就像我一开始说的，拉法叶并没有什么特别独特的地方，这些结果对大多数美国城市来说都是典型的。

cues.en: Well, I guess in Lafayette, the suburban sprawl is built on former wetlands which results in unusually high cost for storm water management, but otherwise, it's pretty typical.
cues.zh: 我想在Lafayette，郊区的无序扩张是建在曾经的湿地上，导致雨水管理成本异常高昂，但除此之外，还挺典型的。

cues.en: So let's look at another city that's not literally built on a swamp, Eugene, Oregon.
cues.zh: 那我们来看看另一个并非真正建在沼泽上的城市，俄勒冈州的Eugene。

cues.en: Here's the urban three map of taxable value per acre. Once again, downtown is clearly visible.
cues.zh: 这是每英亩应税价值的城市三维地图。市中心又一次清晰可见。

cues.en: And here's the three d map of revenue compared to expenses.
cues.zh: 这是收入与支出对比的三维地图。

cues.en: It's still obvious where downtown is, but you might be wondering about this little bump over here.
cues.zh: 市中心依然很明显，但你可能会好奇这边这个小凸起。

cues.en: This is Crescent Village, a modern mixed use development because once again, these kinds of mixed use walkable neighborhoods financially outperform car dependent suburbia
cues.zh: 这是Crescent Village，一个现代混合用途开发项目，因为这类混合用途、适合步行的社区在财务上又一次跑赢了依赖汽车的郊区，

cues.en: every single time.
cues.zh: 每一次都是。

cues.en: By the way, here's what that three d map of Eugene looks like from below. The red spikes correspond almost perfectly to modern car centric suburban developments.
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，这是Eugene那张三维地图从下方看的样子。红色尖峰几乎完美对应现代以汽车为中心的郊区开发。

cues.en: A visual reminder that car dependent suburbia is being subsidized by productive urban places.
cues.zh: 这是一个视觉提醒：依赖汽车的郊区正在被高产的城市场所补贴。

cues.en: The data from Urban three makes the subsidies visible and it makes it very clear who's subsidizing who.
cues.zh: Urban three的数据让这些补贴变得可见，也让人非常清楚谁在补贴谁。

cues.en: In Eugene, Urban three analyzed nine categories of development, residential,
cues.zh: 在Eugene，Urban three分析了九类开发项目：住宅、

cues.en: mixed use, and commercial in low, medium, and high density.
cues.zh: 混合用途，以及商业，分为低、中、高密度。

cues.en: And here's what the average revenue for the city looked like after taking into account the servicing of these properties.
cues.zh: 这是考虑了这些物业的服务成本后，城市平均收入的样子。

cues.en: In the case of Eugene, the low density suburban housing is being subsidized by everything else.
cues.zh: 以尤金为例，低密度郊区住房一直在靠其他一切来补贴。

cues.en: People may look at this and say, but I want to live in a low density single family home and that's fine, but only if you're also willing to pay for it. But there's a bigger problem. This is what the land use map looks like for Eugene, Oregon. The majority of land is zoned exclusively for single family residential,
cues.zh: 人们看到这个可能会说，但我就是想住在低密度独栋住宅里，这没问题，但前提是你也愿意为此买单。但还有一个更大的问题。这就是俄勒冈州尤金的土地利用图。大部分土地被划为独栋住宅专用区，

cues.en: which means that the majority of properties in the city are a net negative to city finances.
cues.zh: 这意味着城市里大多数房产对城市财政都是净负贡献。

cues.en: And this is a pretty typical result for an American city.
cues.zh: 而这对于美国城市来说是相当典型的结果。

cues.en: When you see results like this, is there any surprise that American cities are broke?
cues.zh: 看到这样的结果，美国城市破产还有什么好奇怪的？

cues.en: Here's the tax revenue per acre for South Bend, Indiana.
cues.zh: 这是印第安纳州南本德的每英亩税收收入。

cues.en: See if you can spot downtown.
cues.zh: 看看你能不能找到市中心。

cues.en: Or here in Charleston, South Carolina.
cues.zh: 或者南卡罗来纳州的查尔斯顿。

cues.en: Or in Saint Paul, Minnesota.
cues.zh: 或者明尼苏达州的圣保罗。

cues.en: And here's the entire state of New Hampshire with all of the traditional downtown neighborhoods clearly visible.
cues.zh: 这里是整个新罕布什尔州，所有传统市中心街区都清晰可见。

cues.en: In every case, in every region Urban three is analyzed, traditional
cues.zh: 在每一个案例中，在城市三维分析所涉及的每一个区域，传统的

cues.en: mixed use walkable neighborhoods dramatically outperform car centric suburbia.
cues.zh: 混合用途、适合步行的街区都远远胜过以汽车为中心的郊区。

cues.en: But in North America, we've made it difficult or even impossible to build new neighborhoods this way because of modern zoning and other car centric regulations.
cues.zh: 但在北美，由于现代分区和其他以汽车为中心的法规，我们让以这种方式建设新街区变得困难甚至不可能。

cues.en: Of course, these mathematics apply outside of America as well. Here's a map of Auckland, New Zealand.
cues.zh: 当然，这些数学规律在美国以外同样适用。这是新西兰奥克兰的地图。

cues.en: You can clearly see the increased city revenue along transit lines.
cues.zh: 你可以清楚地看到，沿线城市的收入增加了。

cues.en: And you need to zoom out significantly to see downtown because it is so financially productive.
cues.zh: 你需要大幅缩小视图才能看到市中心，因为它的经济产出太高了。

cues.en: So what do we do with this information?
cues.zh: 那么，我们该如何利用这些信息呢？

cues.en: Well, our cities, through their policies,
cues.zh: 嗯，我们的城市，通过它们的政策，

cues.en: can decide what kind of developments they encourage.
cues.zh: 可以决定鼓励什么样的开发项目。

cues.en: The city of Guelph in Ontario, Canada, not far from my hometown, is an excellent example.
cues.zh: 加拿大安大略省的圭尔夫市，离我的家乡不远，就是一个很好的例子。

cues.en: Guelph needed more room and like all Canadian cities, they were considering expanding their borders and sprawling.
cues.zh: 圭尔夫需要更多空间，和所有加拿大城市一样，他们考虑过扩张边界、无序蔓延。

cues.en: But after running this kind of ROI analysis, they decided to focus on infill developments by making it cheaper and easier for developers to create buildings that encourage walkable neighborhoods.
cues.zh: 但在做了这种投资回报分析之后，他们决定专注于填空式开发，让开发商更容易、更便宜地建造鼓励步行街区的建筑。

cues.en: Like this one.
cues.zh: 就像这个。

cues.en: Here's what the revenue per hectare Because Canada looked like for Guelph in 2013.
cues.zh: 这是2013年圭尔夫每公顷收入的样子。

cues.en: Not bad. In general, Canadian cities are better with their finances than American cities.
cues.zh: 不错。总的来说，加拿大城市在财务上比美国城市做得好。

cues.en: But here it is in 2016
cues.zh: 但到了2016年，

cues.en: and in 2019.
This is what a financially solvent city looks like.
cues.zh: 这就是一个财务上稳健的城市该有的样子。

cues.en: So which path will the financially struggling American cities choose for their future?
cues.zh: 那么，那些财务上挣扎的美国城市会选择哪条路作为未来呢？

cues.en: They can decide to make it easy to build mixed use walkable neighborhoods, making good use of land and encouraging walking, cycling, and public transit.
cues.zh: 他们可以决定让建造混合用途的步行街区变得容易，善用土地，鼓励步行、骑行和公共交通。

cues.en: Or they can build more of this garbage and go bankrupt.
cues.zh: 或者他们可以建造更多这种垃圾，然后破产。

cues.en: Seems like a pretty easy decision to me.
cues.zh: 对我来说，这似乎是个相当容易的决定。

cues.en: I'd like to thank my supporters on Patreon who pay me to mathematically annihilate the suburbs in three d.
cues.zh: 感谢我在 Patreon 上的支持者，他们付钱让我在三维空间里用数学彻底消灭郊区。

cues.en: If you like this kind of content, check out Strong Towns in Urban three. And if you really like this kind of video, visit patreon.com/notchasbikes.
cues.zh: 如果你喜欢这类内容，去看看《Strong Towns》和《Urban Three》。如果你真的很喜欢这类视频，请访问 patreon.com/notchasbikes。
